title: Generic zero-section vanishing for a principal divisor in a normal scheme
statement:
Use the finite coefficient and nearby-cycle specialization conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] and [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type $k$-scheme, meaning that all its local rings are integrally closed domains. Let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $i:Z=V(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be its scheme-theoretic zero subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be a bounded constructible etale complex [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and assume $i^*M=0$. Form the Rees lift $\widetilde X_Z$ and its special fibre $N_{Z/X}$ with zero section $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ as in [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. For every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $Z$ and every geometric point $\bar\xi$ over $\xi$, one has
$$(z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M)_{\bar\xi}=0.$$
Equivalently, the bounded constructible complex $z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M$ vanishes on a dense open subset of every component of $Z$. The scheme $Z$ may be nonreduced, and no finite Tor amplitude assumption on $M$ is required.

In particular this applies to $X=\mathbf A^m_k$ with $m\geq1$ and the coordinate hyperplane $Z=V(x_m)$.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, using the defect cone of §3, with §3.2.2(I) and Lemma 3.1.3 (the contractible rank-one case)

proof.text: Fix a generic point ξ of a component of Z. Normal finite-type X has disjoint irreducible components, so work on the component containing ξ. If f is identically zero there, Z=X locally and i^*M=0 makes M=0, giving the assertion. If f is a unit, Z is empty. Otherwise Z is an effective principal Cartier divisor. Shrinking about ξ, the generic smooth-coordinate reduction gives Z=V(g^r) with g:X→A¹ smooth. All later shrinkings contain ξ.

For this pair let C_{X,Z}(M)=cone(z^*sp_{\widetilde X_Z}M→i^*M), using the canonical map (1.8). Take the cone on the functorial derived models supplied by the nearby-cycle finiteness node; this gives the triangulated defect functor. The defect-comparison node supplies its proper and smooth comparisons and localization isomorphism.

For any finite constant module sheaf L_X, the smooth-coordinate reduction and smooth defect comparison reduce C_{X,Z}(L_X) to C_{A¹,V(x^r)}(L_{A¹}), which vanishes by the constant-defect node. The localization isomorphism in the defect-comparison node then gives C_{X,Z}(j_!L_U)=C_{X,Z}(L_X)=0. This proves the constant-on-the-complement case, allowing arbitrary finite constant modules and nonreduced thickening r≥1.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3 proof, constant-sheaf case; Example 3.1.2 and Lemma 3.1.3

proof.text: For a constructible sheaf F with i^*F=0, the finite-cover sequence node allows shrinking about ξ so F=j_!G with G finite locally constant. Prove by induction on the integer a≥-1, simultaneously for all such G, that H^a(C(j_!G)) vanishes at ξ. For a<-1 it vanishes already: the defining formula sp=i^*Rj_* on an exact inverse-image pullback of F has no negative cohomology, and C is the cone of a map to the sheaf i^*F=0. Choose the finite etale trivialization and its finite normalization q:X′→X from the sequence node. Step 3 on each component of normal X′ gives generic vanishing for C_{X′,Z′}(j′_!p^*G), since p^*G is constant. The sequence node makes q finite and each point over ξ generic in Z′. Its finite-stalk formula and exactness identify (Rq_{Z*}C_{X′,Z′}(j′_!p^*G))_{ξ} with a finite product of zero stalk complexes. Proper comparison for q thus gives (C(q_*j′_!p^*G))_{ξ}=0. Apply the triangulated defect functor to the short exact sequence 0→j_!G→q_*j′_!p^*G→j_!G′→0. Its cohomology sequence identifies H^a(C(j_!G)) at ξ with H^{a-1}(C(j_!G′)) at ξ, which vanishes by induction. Thus every cohomology stalk of C(F) vanishes.

For bounded constructible M, the exact restriction i^* sends its cohomology sheaves to zero since i^*M=0. The defect functor is triangulated by the comparison node, so the successive triangles τ≤b-1 M→τ≤b M→H^b(M)[-b] of the truncation definition reduce C(M) at ξ, in finitely many steps, to Step 4; hence C(M) has zero stalk. Since C(M)=cone(z^*sp(M)→0), its vanishing implies the required zero-section specialization stalk vanishes. Constructibility and boundedness of specialization from the nearby-cycle finiteness node show that finitely many cohomology supports avoid ξ, so after shrinking they vanish on a dense open of the component. This proves the equivalent formulation and the affine-space special case.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-a4f6bff45 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, the 4 new nodes, every cited statement and the parent's proof, plus Varshavsky math/0505564: §1.3.2-1.3.3, §1.4 ((1.8), Lemma 1.4.3), §3 intro, Example 3.1.2, Lemmas 3.1.3-3.1.4, Lemma 3.2.1, 3.2.2(I)-(III), Claim 3.2.3 and Remark 3.2.5. The item matches Claim 3.2.3: same hypotheses, nonreduced Z allowed, no Tor finiteness, etale D^b_c(X,A_{E,n}) coefficients, BC^* along the zero-section lift. The proof stays on the unit's normal-cone route. Steps: (1) the components of a normal X are disjoint; the cases f=0 and f a unit are handled; otherwise f is a nonzerodivisor and the smooth-reduction child applies. (2)-(3) smooth comparison along g with Z=g^{-1}V(x^r), the constant-defect child, then localization. (4) the base case a<-1 holds since C=z^*sp[1] sits in degrees >=-1; the induction is simultaneous over local systems G on one U; the middle term vanishes at xi by proper comparison along the finite map q, the finite-stalk product and Step 3 on normal X'. (5) truncation triangles, then the dense-open form by constructibility. Children: generic smooth reduction (height-one point, DVR, uniformizer, perfect k) is true; constant defect on A^1 with V(x^r) holds for any finite module and any r; the defect comparison is true; the finite-cover sequence is true clause by clause (q_*j'_!=j_!p_*, the bad locus avoids xi). No restatement, no circular split, no duplicate (searched contractible, uniformizer/DVR, V(x^r), relative normalization, constant family). No SGA cited, no cycle. Fixes: (a) lem-trf-dnc-defect-proper-smooth-comparison used an undefined 'canonical zero-section map' on non-ctf D^b_c. I made it explicit as BC^* for Z_D->X~_Z followed by the inverse of the constant-family unit, now asserted invertible on D^b_c (Varshavsky 1.3.3(a)/Remark 3.2.5, also proved in the parent's proof). This is needed for C(i_*N)=0 and for the constant-defect child with non-flat L. (b) lem-trf-dnc-generic-local-system-devissage listed 4 lemma ids in stmt_deps that its statement does not use; I removed them.
